sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the FIR in question has been lodged with the delay of about 18 months.
He submitted that the relationship (if any) between the applicant and the prosecutrix was that of consent.

3. Learned counsel argued that the prosecutrix had gone with the present applicant on multiple occasions at various places and hence, if any forceful sexual assault was committed by the present applicant, she could have easily raised alarm or cry for help.
4.
He contended that the FIR in question is false and has been lodged vindictively and prayed that the present applicant be enlarged on bail.

5. Learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application by submitting that in her statement recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of the Cr.P.C., the prosecutrix had leveled clear allegation of forceful sexual assault upon the applicant and thus, no indulgence be granted.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
7.
It is to be noted that there is a major discrepancy in the version of the prosecutrix in the FIR, in her statement given under Sections 161 and those given under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C.
The story narrated by her is dissimilar and there are various differences and contradictions in the events and places.
That apart, had there been commission of any forceful sexual assault, nothing prevented the prosecutrix to at least inform her husband and other relatives about the said incident.

8. The fact that the FIR in question came to be lodged belatedly (after about 18 months), is fatal to the prosecution's case and [2024:RJ-JD:2717] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-16216/2023] further, because the co-accused (Subhas Chandra) has been enlarged on bail by this Court vide order dated 17.11.2023 in S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application No.13826/2023, this Court deems it just and proper to grant bail to the accused-applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C.
9.

entities.text: S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application No.13826/2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Consequently, the bail application filed under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. is allowed.

The applicant - Rohit Kumar @ Duryodhan @ Dharmendra S/o Om Prakash arrested in connection with FIR No.296/2023, registered at Police Station Mahila Thana (Hanumangarh), District Hanumangarh shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
10. Applicant shall be required to appear before that Court on all dates of hearing and as and when called upon to do so.
11. Needless to mention that the above observations made by this Court are on the basis of material so far produced before the Court.

These are only prima-facie observations and the same shall however, not come in the way of the trial Court to take independent view of the matter, based on ocular and oral evidence, while finally deciding the case.

(DINESH MEHTA),J 76-akansha/-
